summary: This note describes Peqin Castle, a castle in Peqin, Albania. It traces the site's origins to the Roman period, when the city was known as Clodiana in an Illyrian-inhabited territory, and links the foundations to the construction of the Via Egnatia. The castle was later rebuilt and expanded during the Turkish occupation, when control passed to the local fief's Sipahi, who added a palace and a harem; its last resident was Demir Pasha.
one_line: Peqin Castle is a Albanian castle in Peqin with Roman-era foundations, later expanded under Ottoman rule and last occupied by Demir Pasha.
key_facts: Peqin Castle is a castle in Peqin, Albania.
In Roman times the city of Peqin was known by the name Clodiana.
The foundations of Peqin Castle are thought to date from the Roman period.
The Roman-era foundations are thought to be from the time of the construction of the Via Egnatia.
The walls of Peqin Castle at one point had a height of around the figure given in the note, with no value stated.
The castle was later rebuilt and expanded during the Turkish occupation of Albania.
During the Turkish occupation, control of the castle passed to the Sipahi (lord) of the local fief.
The Sipahi of the local fief added a palace and a harem to the castle.
The last resident of Peqin Castle was Demir Pasha.
